The retrieved evidence consistently indicates that cloud computing is at least as secure as, and often more secure than, traditional on-premises IT systems. Multiple sources cite Gartner’s estimate that public cloud workloads suffer at least 60% fewer security incidents than traditional data centers [d1,d3]. Alert Logic data show on-premises environments experience more attacks on average than cloud service provider environments [d2]. Major cloud providers employ specialized cybersecurity personnel and advanced defenses, making them far more secure than most on-premises setups [d7]. SaaS providers implement robust controls including encryption, multifactor authentication, and continuous testing, positioning cloud security as equal to or better than on-premises software [d8].
